name: Hugh Mundell
hook: A lawyer's teenage son who met Augustus Pablo at a studio, wrote a five-star debut album while still a minor, and was shot dead at 21.
blurb: Hugh Mundell met the producer Augustus Pablo at a Kingston studio as a young teenager, and his whole recording career ran through Pablo. Between 1976 and 1978 the two recorded what became Mundell's first album, 'Africa Must Be Free By 1983' (1978), released on Pablo's Rockers International label when Mundell was still only 16. He wrote every song on it himself. It got a five-star review from Rolling Stone and is now regarded as a landmark of roots reggae. He kept recording with Pablo, including the 1979 album 'Blackman's Foundation'. On 14 October 1983 he was shot dead in his car in Kingston, aged 21. Junior Reid, who was in the back seat and later had his own career, including a spell as the singer of Black Uhuru, saw it happen.

signatureTracks.title: Africa Must Be Free By 1983
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: His debut album, written entirely by a teenager and produced by Augustus Pablo, and the record that established him.

signatureTracks.title: Blackman's Foundation
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: His second album with Pablo, co-produced by Mundell himself as he grew into the studio relationship.
